note: Material tuning for every VtMB garment, in Chaos's own terms. Project-authored remaster
content: nothing here is copied out of the user's game. What VtMB itself authored --
particle rest positions, the anchored prefix, the constraint graph, the collider set and the
per-garment gravity scale -- is read at build time from the gitignored export sidecar and is
never restated here.
This file exists because the authored payload states a garment's SHAPE and its SOLVE, and
states nothing about what it is MADE OF. VtMB's solver had no notion of a material: no
density, no friction, no thickness. Chaos does, and a coat that is leather has to be told so.
That judgement is a reading of the garment -- its name, the bones it hangs from, its drop and
footprint -- and it is recorded per garment below rather than derived, because no rule
recovers `heavy leather` from a vertex count.
Two authored measurements DO inform the numbers, and each garment's note names them:
bend slack k   VtMB's compression-only constraint set is the bend diagonals of the same
mesh, one-sided, with rest length `actual / k`. So the spring is inert until
the diagonal folds to 1/k of rest, and 1/k is how much resistance the artist
asked for. k runs 1.00 (stiffest, resists at rest) to 31.62 (Jeanette alone,
effectively free). It is the strongest single signal for `bend_stiffness`.
stretch s      The distance set's per-edge relaxation factor. It is NOT transplanted:
VtMB solved that set twice per substep across 30 substeps plus 15 settling
passes, so the same factor buys far less convergence in our budget. It is
used as an ORDERING between garments, compressed into a range that holds.
Resolution is `defaults` <- `materials[<name>]` <- the garment entry, each layer overriding
by key. `defaults` declares every key, so a material or a garment states only what differs.
Tuning the whole corpus means editing `defaults` or one material; tuning one garment means
adding a key to its entry. A stem with no entry resolves to `fallback_material` and is
reported, so an untuned garment is visible rather than silently average.
Stiffnesses are Chaos's legacy PBD 0..1 relaxation factors, which is what
`UChaosClothConfig::EdgeStiffnessWeighted` / `BendingStiffnessWeighted` feed. They are NOT
the physical-unit XPBD values (stiffness 100, kg/s^2) quoted by the Dataflow editor and by
most current tutorials; those belong to a different property set and must not be pasted here.
`density` is Chaos's own kg-scale, and the reference points are the engine's own tooltip:
melton wool 0.7, heavy leather 0.6, polyurethane 0.5, denim 0.4, light leather 0.3,
cotton 0.2, silk 0.1.
The leash is ours, not VtMB's -- the retail solve has no per-particle displacement limit at
all and holds the surface on the body with its constraint graph alone. Chaos needs one at
real-time substep counts, so `leash_reach_fraction` scales it by each particle's own geodesic
distance to the pinned set, measured over the simulation mesh. A waistband particle therefore
gets a tight leash and a hem particle a loose one, and one number means the same thing on a
35 cm necktie and a 228 cm cloak.
Shared across every garment. `substep_target_ms` and `max_substeps` are VtMB's own clock --
`N = min(30, round(elapsed * 300))` -- and Chaos reproduces it as
`clamp(round(dt * 1000 / substep_target_ms), 1, max_substeps)`, so 60 fps runs 5 substeps
and the cap only binds below 10 fps. Iteration counts are the real budget knob: Epic's
guidance for cloth on many NPCs is 1 for both, the engine default for the max is 10. Two
sits above the floor because several garments below are authored genuinely stretchy, and
raising it is the first thing to try if a long skirt sags at the hem.
Every key the build reads, with the value a garment gets when neither its material nor its
own entry says otherwise. `area_stiffness` is 0 deliberately: VtMB authors exactly two
constraint sets, edges and bend diagonals, and no area-preservation set at all -- so the
engine's default of 1 buys a constraint the garment was never designed around and charges
for it every substep.

heavy_leather_coat.note: Full-length leather duster or cloak. Holds a line, sweeps the legs, swings slowly.

canvas_coat.note: Cloth or waxed-canvas long coat. Lighter and more mobile than leather; flares more.

formal_wool_robe.note: Ceremonial robe, heavy wool. Stiffest thing in the cast: it must not flutter.

formal_gown.note: Structured floor-length gown. Narrow, heavy, keeps its silhouette around the legs.

evening_gown.note: Satin or light crepe gown. Drapes and folds readily; low bend is the whole look.

heavy_skirt.note: Velvet, wool or heavy cotton skirt. Full cut, folds under its own weight.

light_skirt.note: Short or lightweight skirt. Little bending resistance, quick to settle.

note: A pleated wool miniskirt, and the loosest bend in the game by a factor of thirty. The
authored k of 31.62 means the bend spring never engages at all; 0.08 rather than 0.03
gives the pleats just enough memory to read as pleats instead of as a hanging sheet.
A loose silk dress panel hanging off a thigh. Silk is nearly inextensible and almost
unresisting in bend, so edge stays at 1 while bend goes well below the authored 0.45.
A necktie: a narrow interlined strip that hangs straight and folds only at the knot. Not
limp -- the interlining is why a tie keeps its line -- so bend sits mid-range. No CCD:
it lives on the sternum and never meets a fast collider.
Fur and hair, not cloth. VtMB authors these at full stretch relaxation on every edge --
a strand does not lengthen -- over a shallow fringe that sways only at the tips. Light,
short-leashed, and no CCD: nothing here moves far enough in a substep to tunnel.
A bead cord held between two hands. Inextensible, heavy for its size, and with four free
particles there is nothing here to drape -- the settings exist to keep it inert and cheap
rather than to shape it.

beckett.note: Coat tails below the waist, 75 cm drop off pelvis and spine, colliders on the legs only. Authored k = 1.00 (stiffest) at 1.0 g, the lightest gravity in the cast -- a stiff leather panel that lags behind the walk rather than swinging.

blueblood_female.note: `bbfemflap`: a dress flap off both thighs and the pelvis, 69 cm. Authored k = 2.24 -- slack bend -- at 6 g, which is VtMB weighing a light panel down so it stays on the legs. Shares its 30 x 46 cm source mesh with mingxiao.

buch.note: Full-length duster off the shoulders and clavicles, 130 cm drop, 17 rings, colliders down the whole leg column. Authored k = 1.20 at 1.5 g: a heavy coat deliberately given low gravity so it flares.

bum_male.note: The smallest cloth in the game: 11 particles, 7 triangles, a 40 cm strip off Spine2. A ragged tie or scarf, so slightly heavier and limper than a pressed one.

elite_hunter.note: Society of Leopold long coat, 126 cm drop, 16 rings, with a neck collider as well as the leg column. Authored k = 1.20 at 1.5 g -- the same heavy-but-flaring recipe as buch.

goth_female.note: Full flared skirt, 69 cm wide and 88 cm long, 12 rings. Authored k = 1.41 at 2 g. Velvet weight: it should fold in on itself and swing wide rather than flutter.

jeanette.note: The showcase garment and the one true outlier: a 16 cm drop over only 4 rings, 60 cm wide, at 5 g with authored k = 31.62 -- thirty times slacker in bend than anything else in the cast. Short, heavy and completely free to flounce.

malkavian_female_armor_0.note: Short hip skirt, 20 cm drop over 5 rings, 66 cm wide. Authored k = 1.20 at 3 g -- stiffer in bend than its size suggests, so it flares rather than clinging.

malkavian_male_armor_3.note: Long coat with a separate fur trim material, pinned at the spine AND both upper arms so the lapels move with the sleeves. 128 cm drop, 17 rings, authored k = 1.41 at 3 g.

mingxiao.note: `Mingfrontdress` + `Mingfbackdress`: two separate panels pinned to the thighs only, which is a qipao with thigh-high side slits. Authored k = 2.24 at 6 g -- slack bend, heavy pull, so the panels swing between the legs and settle fast.

nosferatu_female_armor_2.note: `NosF2Skirt`, named as such: 82 cm off the pelvis alone, 12 rings, authored k = 1.41 at 3 g.

prostitute_2_ref.note: Three pieces -- a front torso panel, a back torso panel and a short skirt -- pinned across the waist and chest. 46 cm, authored k = 1.41 at 2 g. Cheap light fabric.

regent.note: Ceremonial robe, 118 cm off the shoulders, with a radius-37 collider sphere on the head for the hood. Authored k = 1.00 -- stiffest -- at 4 g. Shares its 298-particle mesh with ventrue_male_armor_3, which VtMB tuned softer; the difference in material here is that authored difference.

rosa.note: A 135 cm line, 1.3 cm wide, pinned at the fingertips of BOTH hands -- a bead cord or rosary held taut by the oracle. 28 of 32 particles pinned, ring depth 1, no colliders. There is almost nothing to simulate and the tuning is there to keep it that way.

security_guard_skinny.note: A 35 cm necktie, 8 cm wide, off the sternum in 10 segments. Byte-identical cloth to stan_gimble.

sheriff.note: The full-length hooded cloak, pinned at the HEAD and shoulders on a 2.3 m body: 228 cm of drop over 17 rings, the longest in the game. Authored k = 1.20 at 3 g. The leash cap is raised because a garment this long genuinely does swing that far.

stan_gimble.note: The same 36-particle necktie as security_guard_skinny, on the prosthetics clerk.

tin_can_bill.note: Almost entirely hair -- 255 of the 278 claimed vertices are `TinCanHair` -- off the head, with token body and head cloth beside it. 67 cm drop, 4 rings, full stretch relaxation on every authored edge.

toreador_female_armor_2.note: Pinned at the spine and the bust bones, which makes it a strapless bodice: 91 cm drop, narrow at 37 x 26 cm, 17 rings. Authored k = 1.41 at 4 g. Toreador, so satin rather than wool.

toreador_female_armor_3.note: Narrow and short at 32 x 24 x 48 cm over only 4 rings -- coarse, 12 cm segments. Authored k = 1.00 at 4 g: a stiff straight skirt that holds its line rather than gathering.

tremere_female_armor_0.note: The widest garment in the cast at 80 cm across, 88 cm long, 12 rings. Authored k = 1.20 at 3 g -- a full robe skirt with real body to it.

tremere_female_armor_2.note: Narrow mid-length skirt, 28 x 22 x 51 cm, 8 rings, authored k = 1.20 at 3 g. Same cloth as tremere_female_armor_0 in a much tighter cut, so the leash is capped down with it.

tremere_female_armor_3.note: `TremFA3cuffstuff`, definition 0: the hanging bell sleeves, pinned at both ulnae and a forearm, 124 cm apart with the arms out and 32 cm of drop each. Same wool as the robe but it has to swing off a moving forearm, so bend comes down by half and the leash is short.

`TremFA3body`, definition 1: the floor-length robe skirt off the pelvis, 102 cm drop over 11 rings. Authored k = 1.20 at 3 g. This model is the only one carrying two cloth definitions, which is why 28 characters produce 29 assets.

ventrue_female_armor_0.note: Slim long skirt, 34 x 25 x 83 cm, 11 rings, authored k = 1.41 at 4 g.

ventrue_female_armor_2.note: Long narrow skirt off the thighs, 80 cm drop, authored k = 1.00 at 6 g -- the stiffest bend paired with the heaviest gravity. Ventrue formality: it barely moves.

ventrue_female_armor_3.note: 119 cm off the spine over 16 rings, authored k = 1.00 at 6 g. Stiffest and heaviest in the cast, and simultaneously the loosest measured stretch relaxation -- a heavy gown that drapes deeply without ever losing its silhouette.

ventrue_male_armor_3.note: `newMaleVENArmr3bcoat`: the identical 298-particle, 496-triangle coat mesh the Regent wears, but authored at k = 1.41 and 3 g against the Regent's k = 1.00 and 4 g. Same garment, deliberately softer and lighter, so it takes cloth rather than heavy wool.

wolf_form_2.note: `wolfformbody` + `wolfformtailneck` + `wolfformfurstuff`: 172 cm along a quadruped's body axis with 278 of 480 particles pinned and a fringe only 3 rings deep. Full stretch relaxation on every edge and no colliders at all.
